methodology.eligibility: Active Nursing eligibility is calculated through QuestionEligibilityService::forExam using the production QuestionEligibilityIndex; canonical topic keywords never determine board ownership.
methodology.risk: P0/P1/P2 and risk categories are review-order flags. They are heuristic screens based on canonical concept, stem, options and rationale; they do not declare a question clinically unsafe or verified.
methodology.source_status: Status is copied from the current source registry for linked source IDs. A status is not proof that a source supports this question or that a claim is current.
methodology.potential_defects: Automated flags identify fields or patterns for human audit only. They are not adjudicated question defects.

Longitudinal lie with cephalic presentation

Begin pushing regardless of cervical dilation
Apply fundal pressure to rotate the fetus
Correlate the position with fetal heart-rate findings and labor progress

questions.STEM: A newborn is being placed for routine care. Which position is represented by the diagram and best supports airway alignment while the infant is observed?

Prone with the face turned into the mattress
Trendelenburg with the neck hyperextended
Sitting unsupported with the chin on the chest

questions.STEM: A client with acute dyspnea is being positioned before oxygen therapy is reassessed. Which position is shown and is most appropriate to improve chest expansion?

High-Fowler position
Prone position
Lithotomy position
questions.ANSWER_KEY: High-Fowler position
questions.RATIONALE: Elevating the head and trunk reduces diaphragmatic pressure and supports lung expansion. Flat or unrelated procedural positions do not address the immediate respiratory need.

Intravenous insertion in the antecubital fossa
Rectal or perineal examination
Measurement of standing balance
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Rectal or perineal examination

Disconnect the tubing briefly to verify urine flow
Rest the catheter tip on the edge of the sterile field
Keep the collection bag below bladder level without allowing the tubing or field to touch nonsterile surfaces
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Keep the collection bag below bladder level without allowing the tubing or field to touch nonsterile surfaces
questions.RATIONALE: The diagram shows a closed drainage path with the bag below the bladder. Keeping the system closed and dependent reduces contamination and backflow; placing it on the bed or disconnecting it breaks safe technique.

Gown

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: The side-lying client has pressure points labeled A, B, and C. Which nursing action best reduces injury risk before leaving the client in this position?
OPTIONS: Place a firm object directly under every labeled point
Pad and reassess each bony contact point, keeping alignment supported
Leave the client unsupported because side-lying removes pressure
Massage reddened skin vigorously to restore circulation
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Pad and reassess each bony contact point, keeping alignment supported
questions.RATIONALE: The labeled contacts identify areas needing off-loading and skin reassessment. Hard objects and vigorous massage can injure tissue, while unsupported alignment increases pressure and shear.

questions.STEM: Which sleep arrangement shown supports current safe-sleep teaching for a healthy infant?
OPTIONS: Prone on a soft pillow with a blanket over the face
Side-lying with rolled towels around the body
Supine on a firm, flat surface without loose bedding
Supine in an inclined seat for overnight sleep
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Supine on a firm, flat surface without loose bedding
questions.RATIONALE: The diagram depicts a firm, flat sleep surface and supine orientation. Pillows, loose bedding, prone sleep, and routine overnight seating increase avoidable risk.

Advance the tube until the client coughs
Rely only on the external length mark
Confirm placement using the facility-approved method before introducing the feeding

Respiratory rate rising from 20 to 30/min with falling oxygen saturation
Pulse changing from 82 to 88/min
Blood pressure changing from 124/76 to 120/74 mmHg
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Respiratory rate rising from 20 to 30/min with falling oxygen saturation

OPTIONS: The lowest value proves acute malnutrition
The highest value proves the child is overweight
The pattern should be plotted and assessed over time rather than judged from one value
No follow-up is needed when one value is within range
questions.ANSWER_KEY: The pattern should be plotted and assessed over time rather than judged from one value
questions.RATIONALE: Growth assessment depends on a plotted trend and the child’s age, sex, and clinical context. One isolated measurement cannot establish a diagnosis or eliminate follow-up.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A postpartum client saturates a perineal pad in 15 minutes and has a boggy fundus. What is the nurse’s priority action?
OPTIONS: Offer oral fluids and reassess in two hours
Ambulate the client to improve circulation
Document the finding as an expected postpartum change
Massage the fundus while assessing the client and calling for help per protocol
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Massage the fundus while assessing the client and calling for help per protocol
questions.RATIONALE: Heavy bleeding with a boggy uterus suggests uterine atony. Immediate fundal assessment/massage and escalation address the life-threatening priority; delay and ambulation are unsafe.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client receiving IV potassium reports burning at the site; the area is cool and swollen. What should the nurse do first?
OPTIONS: Stop the infusion and assess the IV site before further action
Increase the rate to dilute the medication
Apply pressure and continue the infusion
Flush forcefully to clear the catheter
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Stop the infusion and assess the IV site before further action
questions.RATIONALE: Coolness and swelling suggest infiltration or another IV complication. Stopping the infusion prevents additional harm while the site is assessed; increasing or forcefully flushing is unsafe.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: Four clients arrive for assessment. Which client should the nurse see first?
OPTIONS: A client requesting a routine dressing change
A client with new stridor and increasing work of breathing
A client reporting chronic mild back pain
A client awaiting discharge paperwork
questions.ANSWER_KEY: A client with new stridor and increasing work of breathing
questions.RATIONALE: Stridor with increased work of breathing signals possible airway obstruction. Airway threats take priority over routine care, chronic symptoms, and paperwork.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: Before administering a high-alert insulin dose, the nurse finds that the current glucose value and the medication order do not match. What is the safest action?
OPTIONS: Give the ordered dose and document the mismatch afterward
Ask the client to choose the dose
Hold administration and clarify the discrepancy using the required verification process
Delete the order from the medication record
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Hold administration and clarify the discrepancy using the required verification process
questions.RATIONALE: Pause administration and resolve the mismatch through the required verification and escalation process; do not independently change the dose or administer an order that conflicts with the available assessment. WHO’s medication-safety tool supports involving the patient or caregiver in medication conversations with health professionals, but that partnership does not let the patient choose an insulin dose or replace professional order verification.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations

OPTIONS: “There is nothing to worry about.”
“You should think positively.”
“I know exactly how you feel.”
“Tell me what worries you most right now.”
questions.ANSWER_KEY: “Tell me what worries you most right now.”
questions.RATIONALE: The open-ended response acknowledges the emotion and invites assessment. False reassurance, advice, and claiming identical experience can close communication.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client with suspected airborne infection must be transported for an essential diagnostic test. Which plan best reduces transmission?
OPTIONS: Place the client in the required source control and use the prescribed isolation/transport precautions
Remove all precautions because the client leaves the room
Transport through the busiest waiting area to shorten the route
Ask the client to walk unmasked if breathing is difficult
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Place the client in the required source control and use the prescribed isolation/transport precautions
questions.RATIONALE: Essential transport does not eliminate infection controls. Source control and the facility’s prescribed precautions reduce exposure; removing them or using crowded routes increases risk.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A conscious client with diabetes is sweating, shaky, and able to swallow; the bedside glucose is 52 mg/dL. What is the priority intervention?
OPTIONS: Administer the scheduled long-acting insulin
Give the rapid-acting carbohydrate specified by protocol and recheck as directed
Restrict oral intake until the next meal
Place the client flat and leave to obtain the chart
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Give the rapid-acting carbohydrate specified by protocol and recheck as directed
questions.RATIONALE: Symptoms and glucose indicate hypoglycemia in a client able to swallow. Rapid carbohydrate treats the immediate problem, followed by reassessment; insulin and delayed feeding worsen risk.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client after a stroke coughs repeatedly during a sip of water and has a wet voice. Which action is priority?
OPTIONS: Offer larger sips to clear the throat
Place the client supine and continue the meal
Stop oral intake and initiate the prescribed swallowing-safety evaluation
Document the cough as expected
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Stop oral intake and initiate the prescribed swallowing-safety evaluation
questions.RATIONALE: Coughing and a wet voice suggest aspiration risk. Stopping intake protects the airway while swallowing is evaluated; larger sips and continued feeding increase danger.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A hospitalized client has fever, new confusion, respiratory rate 28/min, and a falling blood pressure. Which nursing response is most appropriate?
OPTIONS: Wait for the next scheduled vital-sign round
Give an antipyretic and reassess tomorrow
Encourage ambulation to improve blood pressure
Escalate immediately while supporting airway, breathing, circulation, and obtaining ordered assessments
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Escalate immediately while supporting airway, breathing, circulation, and obtaining ordered assessments
questions.RATIONALE: The combination suggests possible sepsis or shock and requires immediate escalation with ABC support and ordered evaluation. Treating fever alone or delaying reassessment misses the threat.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A newborn’s temperature is falling after bathing. Which action best addresses the immediate problem?
OPTIONS: Dry the newborn, replace wet linens, provide skin-to-skin or approved warming, and reassess
Repeat the bath with cooler water
Place the newborn uncovered near an air vent
Delay feeding and observation until the next shift
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Dry the newborn, replace wet linens, provide skin-to-skin or approved warming, and reassess
questions.RATIONALE: Evaporative heat loss is reduced by drying, warm linens, and approved warming measures. Exposure and delay increase cold stress.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A laboring client has recurrent late fetal heart-rate decelerations. Which initial nursing action is most appropriate while escalating the finding?
OPTIONS: Encourage pushing to shorten labor
Reposition the client laterally, assess the tracing and maternal status, and notify the appropriate clinician
Place the client supine and increase oxytocin
Ignore the pattern if the baseline rate is normal
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Reposition the client laterally, assess the tracing and maternal status, and notify the appropriate clinician
questions.RATIONALE: Late decelerations can indicate impaired uteroplacental oxygen exchange. Lateral positioning, assessment, and escalation address the concern; supine positioning and increasing oxytocin can worsen it.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A community clinic sees a sudden cluster of vomiting illness among people who attended the same event. What should the nurse do first in the investigation?
OPTIONS: Announce the confirmed source before collecting data
Close every facility in the municipality without assessment
Verify the cluster and construct a time, place, and person description while initiating required reporting
Count only clients who required admission
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Verify the cluster and construct a time, place, and person description while initiating required reporting
questions.RATIONALE: Early field investigation checks that reported diagnoses are credible, compares observed cases with an appropriate baseline, and describes cases by time, place, and person. These steps can proceed together when needed, and required reporting continues; do not announce a source before the evidence supports it.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: After an earthquake, which person should receive the most urgent triage attention?
OPTIONS: A person with a minor arm abrasion who is walking
A person asking where the registration desk is
A person with a closed bruise and stable vital signs
A person with severe respiratory distress and uncontrolled bleeding
questions.ANSWER_KEY: A person with severe respiratory distress and uncontrolled bleeding
questions.RATIONALE: Immediate threats to airway, breathing, and circulation take priority in disaster triage. Minor and stable findings can wait for reassessment.

Ask whether the client understands and accept “yes” as sufficient
Give the written instructions without discussion
Demonstrate once while the client watches silently
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Ask the client to demonstrate the technique and correct errors
questions.RATIONALE: Teach-back through demonstration verifies performance rather than assumed understanding. Written material and passive agreement do not show that the client can use the device correctly.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

OPTIONS: Tell the relative because family members have an automatic right to all information
Respect the client’s confidentiality and share information only with authorized consent or a valid care need
Post the diagnosis where the care team can see it
Ask another visitor to explain the diagnosis
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Respect the client’s confidentiality and share information only with authorized consent or a valid care need
questions.RATIONALE: The client controls disclosure of personal health information except where law or a legitimate care need requires otherwise. Family relationship alone does not authorize disclosure.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: The medication administration record shows a scheduled antibiotic was not given and the next dose is due soon. What should the nurse do first?
OPTIONS: Assess the reason and client status, then verify the order and notify the prescriber or pharmacist as required
Double the next dose to replace the missed dose
Document the dose as given to keep the record complete
Ask the client to decide whether the missed dose matters
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Assess the reason and client status, then verify the order and notify the prescriber or pharmacist as required
questions.RATIONALE: A missed medication requires assessment and order-specific follow-up before any replacement dose. Doubling or falsifying the record can cause harm.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: The laboratory trend is reviewed for a client receiving chemotherapy. Which finding requires the most urgent protective response?
OPTIONS: Hemoglobin changing from 104 to 101 g/L without symptoms
Absolute neutrophil count falling to 0.7 ×10⁹/L with a new temperature of 38.1°C
Platelets changing from 180 to 170 ×10⁹/L
Albumin changing from 38 to 36 g/L
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Absolute neutrophil count falling to 0.7 ×10⁹/L with a new temperature of 38.1°C
questions.RATIONALE: Severe neutropenia combined with fever creates an urgent infection risk and requires immediate assessment and escalation. The other trends do not carry the same immediate threat.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client’s neurologic observations are recorded after a head injury. Which pattern should prompt immediate escalation?
OPTIONS: Stable orientation with a headache rated 3/10
Pulse decreasing from 88 to 82/min with warm skin
A new drop in level of consciousness with unequal pupils
One unchanged bruise at the IV site
questions.ANSWER_KEY: A new drop in level of consciousness with unequal pupils
questions.RATIONALE: A deteriorating level of consciousness and unequal pupils suggest worsening neurologic status and possible rising intracranial pressure. This requires immediate escalation, not routine observation.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A postpartum client’s observations are shown. Which interpretation is most concerning?
OPTIONS: A falling pulse with decreasing lochia indicates expected recovery
The temperature trend rules out any uterine complication
Mild fatigue alone confirms severe blood loss
Fever, uterine tenderness, and foul-smelling lochia suggest a postpartum infection requiring prompt evaluation
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Fever, uterine tenderness, and foul-smelling lochia suggest a postpartum infection requiring prompt evaluation
questions.RATIONALE: The combined trend of fever, uterine tenderness, and malodorous lochia is concerning for postpartum infection and requires prompt assessment. It is not explained by normal fatigue or a blood-loss pattern.

questions.STEM: A community vaccination team reviews the coverage data below. Which area should receive the first outreach priority?
OPTIONS: Area B, because its low coverage is concentrated among infants despite adequate adult coverage
Area A, because its adult coverage is highest
Area C, because its total population is largest regardless of coverage
All areas are equivalent because the overall mean is similar
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Area B, because its low coverage is concentrated among infants despite adequate adult coverage
questions.RATIONALE: Outreach should target the subgroup with the most consequential coverage gap, not simply the largest population or overall mean. The table identifies infants in Area B as the priority.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client with renal impairment has the electrolyte trend below. Which action is safest?
OPTIONS: Offer a high-potassium snack to correct the laboratory value
Hold the potassium-containing medication and promptly notify the prescriber while assessing cardiac status
Administer the scheduled potassium without review
Restrict all fluids solely because potassium is elevated
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Hold the potassium-containing medication and promptly notify the prescriber while assessing cardiac status
questions.RATIONALE: A rising potassium level in renal impairment can create dysrhythmia risk. The nurse should pause potassium exposure, assess the client, and escalate; dietary or fluid changes require an individualized order.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: An IV prescription is 1,000 mL over 8 hours using an electronic pump. What rate should the nurse program?
OPTIONS: 80 mL/h
128 mL/h
125 mL/h
questions.ANSWER_KEY: 125 mL/h
questions.RATIONALE: Rate equals volume divided by time: 1,000 mL ÷ 8 h = 125 mL/h. The other values result from reversing or multiplying the inputs.

17 mg
questions.ANSWER_KEY: 17 mg
questions.RATIONALE: Multiply the ordered dose by weight: 0.25 mg/kg × 68 kg = 17 mg. The units cancel correctly; 2.72 mg reflects an incorrect decimal operation.

questions.STEM: A liquid medicine is prescribed at 15 mg/kg for a child weighing 18 kg. The solution contains 75 mg/mL. What volume is required?

1.2 mL
questions.ANSWER_KEY: 3.6 mL
questions.RATIONALE: The required dose is 15×18 = 270 mg. At 75 mg/mL, volume is 270÷75 = 3.6 mL. The dose must be calculated before converting to volume.

7.5 mL
5.0 mL
questions.ANSWER_KEY: 7.5 mL
questions.RATIONALE: The concentration is 50 mg/mL. Therefore 375 mg ÷ 50 mg/mL = 7.5 mL. Using 375 as the volume or using 250 mg as 250 mg/mL gives the distractors.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A 60-kg client produces 240 mL of urine in 8 hours. What is the average urine output in mL/kg/h?

4 mL/kg/h
0.5 mL/kg/h
30 mL/kg/h
questions.ANSWER_KEY: 0.5 mL/kg/h
questions.RATIONALE: First divide volume by time: 240÷8 = 30 mL/h. Then divide by weight: 30÷60 = 0.5 mL/kg/h. Both stages are required for the weight-adjusted rate.

Encourage vigorous walking to lower the pressure
Delay assessment until the next routine prenatal visit
Assess promptly, reduce stimulation, and notify the appropriate clinician for urgent evaluation
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Assess promptly, reduce stimulation, and notify the appropriate clinician for urgent evaluation
questions.RATIONALE: The combined symptoms and changing blood pressure require urgent assessment for a serious hypertensive complication. Reassurance or delay could miss deterioration.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client with diabetes has glucose 420 mg/dL, repeated vomiting, deep rapid respirations, and positive urine ketones. What should the nurse do first?
OPTIONS: Assess airway, breathing, circulation, and urgently escalate for suspected ketoacidosis
Give the scheduled long-acting insulin and leave the client to rest
Offer a high-carbohydrate meal without further assessment
Restrict all fluids until the glucose normalizes
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Assess airway, breathing, circulation, and urgently escalate for suspected ketoacidosis
questions.RATIONALE: Marked hyperglycemia with vomiting, ketones, and deep rapid respirations suggests a metabolic emergency. ABC assessment and urgent escalation are needed; food, fluid restriction, or unsupervised insulin does not address the immediate risk.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client receiving opioids has pH 7.28, PaCO₂ 60 mmHg, HCO₃⁻ 26 mEq/L, increasing drowsiness, and shallow respirations. Which interpretation is best?
OPTIONS: Metabolic alkalosis requiring an antacid
Acute respiratory acidosis with hypoventilation requiring immediate respiratory assessment and escalation
Fully compensated respiratory acidosis requiring no action
Metabolic acidosis caused by excess bicarbonate loss
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Acute respiratory acidosis with hypoventilation requiring immediate respiratory assessment and escalation
questions.RATIONALE: The low pH and elevated PaCO₂ with near-normal bicarbonate indicate acute respiratory acidosis from hypoventilation. Drowsiness and shallow breathing make this an urgent airway and breathing problem.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A nursing assistant reports that a postoperative client is newly dizzy, pale, and asking to stand. Which assignment response is safest?
OPTIONS: Ask the assistant to ambulate the client slowly to test tolerance
Ask the assistant to give an ordered analgesic independently
Tell the assistant to keep the client seated, remain with the client, and notify the nurse immediately
Tell the assistant to document the symptoms after the client walks
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Tell the assistant to keep the client seated, remain with the client, and notify the nurse immediately
questions.RATIONALE: A new change in status requires licensed-nurse assessment and fall prevention. The assistant should not test ambulation or independently administer medication.

questions.STEM: Which client should the nurse assess first at shift change?
OPTIONS: A client requesting a fresh blanket with stable observations
A client awaiting routine discharge instructions
A client with chronic pain at the usual baseline
A client two hours after surgery with increasing abdominal distention and a falling blood pressure
questions.ANSWER_KEY: A client two hours after surgery with increasing abdominal distention and a falling blood pressure
questions.RATIONALE: A new postoperative abdominal change with hypotension may represent bleeding or another acute complication. Stable comfort and discharge requests can wait.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client receiving magnesium sulfate becomes lethargic, has respirations of 10/min, and has absent patellar reflexes. Which action is most appropriate?
OPTIONS: Stop the infusion, support breathing, and notify the clinician immediately for possible toxicity
Increase the infusion because lethargy is expected
Ambulate the client to stimulate the reflexes
Give an oral sedative and reassess later
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Stop the infusion, support breathing, and notify the clinician immediately for possible toxicity
questions.RATIONALE: Respiratory depression and absent reflexes are warning signs of magnesium toxicity. The infusion must be stopped while breathing is supported and urgent help is obtained; increasing it is unsafe.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A newborn is jittery, feeding poorly, and has a low bedside glucose reading. Which sequence is safest?
OPTIONS: Delay treatment until a confirmatory result returns regardless of symptoms
Assess airway and clinical status, follow the neonatal hypoglycemia protocol, provide the indicated treatment, and recheck
Give plain water and repeat the bath later
Document the reading without assessing feeding or temperature
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Assess airway and clinical status, follow the neonatal hypoglycemia protocol, provide the indicated treatment, and recheck
questions.RATIONALE: Symptoms plus a low reading require prompt assessment and protocol-based treatment with reassessment. Delaying or giving water does not address the newborn’s clinical risk.

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client says, “Everyone would be better off without me,” has stopped eating, and gave a friend a bag of medications. What is the priority nursing action?
OPTIONS: Promise to keep the statement secret and leave the client alone to rest
Tell the client to focus on positive thoughts
Stay with the client, remove immediate means when safe, and initiate urgent suicide-risk assessment and support
Schedule a routine counseling appointment next month
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Stay with the client, remove immediate means when safe, and initiate urgent suicide-risk assessment and support
questions.RATIONALE: The statement, behavior change, and medication transfer indicate an immediate safety concern. Continuous safety support and urgent assessment take priority over secrecy, reassurance, or delay.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client with mania speaks rapidly, has slept two hours in three days, and begins spending money impulsively. Which response is most therapeutic?
OPTIONS: Argue about each unrealistic statement until the client agrees
Provide a crowded group activity to use the excess energy
Allow unlimited activity because the behavior is creative
Use brief clear limits, reduce stimulation, assess safety, and offer one focused choice at a time
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Use brief clear limits, reduce stimulation, assess safety, and offer one focused choice at a time
questions.RATIONALE: Mania requires a low-stimulation, structured approach with safety assessment and concise communication. Arguing, crowding, or removing all limits can increase risk.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A community assessment compares household water access and diarrhea reports. Which action should receive first priority?
OPTIONS: Investigate and address the high-risk water source serving Area B while arranging care for symptomatic residents
Distribute the same intervention to every area without comparing exposure
Focus only on the area with the largest population
Wait until every household has a laboratory-confirmed case
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Investigate and address the high-risk water source serving Area B while arranging care for symptomatic residents
questions.RATIONALE: Area B combines the lowest safe-water access with the highest diarrhea rate, making the shared water exposure the priority for investigation and intervention. A population-only approach would ignore the strongest observed association.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A tuberculosis contact investigation finds that several household contacts have symptoms but have not completed evaluation. What is the most appropriate next step?
OPTIONS: Publish the names of symptomatic contacts to increase compliance
Prioritize symptom screening and linkage to diagnostic evaluation while maintaining confidentiality
Close the clinic until every contact is evaluated
Count only contacts who already completed treatment
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Prioritize symptom screening and linkage to diagnostic evaluation while maintaining confidentiality
questions.RATIONALE: Symptomatic contacts need timely assessment and linkage to care. Public disclosure violates confidentiality and counting only completed cases misses people needing evaluation.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A competent adult refuses a recommended procedure after the nurse explains its purpose and risks. What should the nurse do next?
OPTIONS: Threaten discharge unless the client agrees
Ask family to consent on the client’s behalf automatically
Assess understanding and decision-making, respect the refusal, document it, and notify the appropriate clinician
Proceed because the procedure is recommended
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Assess understanding and decision-making, respect the refusal, document it, and notify the appropriate clinician
questions.RATIONALE: Informed refusal requires checking understanding and capacity, respecting the client’s decision, documenting it, and communicating with the care team. A recommendation does not remove autonomy.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: During medication reconciliation, the home list contains two drugs with the same therapeutic purpose and the client reports taking both. What is the safest nursing action?
OPTIONS: Delete one medication from the list based on the nurse’s preference
Tell the client to stop both medications immediately
Record both as current orders without verification
Withhold assumptions, verify the list against current orders and the client’s use, and clarify discrepancies before administration
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Withhold assumptions, verify the list against current orders and the client’s use, and clarify discrepancies before administration
questions.RATIONALE: Duplicate therapy may be intentional or harmful; reconciliation requires verification with the client and prescribing team before changes. Independent deletion or stopping is unsafe.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A client with heart failure has increasing daily weight, new crackles, and decreasing urine output despite the prescribed diuretic. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
OPTIONS: The combined trend suggests worsening fluid retention and requires prompt reassessment and escalation
The weight change is irrelevant if the client denies pain
The crackles prove a respiratory infection without further assessment
The urine output is expected whenever a diuretic is prescribed
questions.ANSWER_KEY: The combined trend suggests worsening fluid retention and requires prompt reassessment and escalation
questions.RATIONALE: Weight gain, crackles, and falling urine output together indicate deteriorating fluid status. The nurse should assess and escalate rather than isolate one finding or assume an unrelated diagnosis.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A nurse catches a wrong-dose selection before administration; the client is unharmed. What response best supports safety?
OPTIONS: Hide the event because no harm occurred
Report the near miss through the safety process and examine how the selection error occurred
Administer the dose anyway because it was already selected
Blame the client for not checking the syringe
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Report the near miss through the safety process and examine how the selection error occurred
questions.RATIONALE: Near-miss reporting supports system learning and prevention even when no harm reaches the client. Concealment prevents correction of the contributing conditions.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A bedbound client has nonblanching redness over the sacrum and poor oral intake. Which plan is most appropriate?
OPTIONS: Massage the reddened area vigorously every hour
Use a donut ring and keep the client in one position
Off-load the area, establish scheduled repositioning and skin checks, and address nutrition and moisture
Wait for an open wound before starting prevention
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Off-load the area, establish scheduled repositioning and skin checks, and address nutrition and moisture
questions.RATIONALE: Nonblanching redness is an early pressure injury warning. Pressure redistribution, reassessment, moisture control, and nutrition support are needed before tissue breakdown progresses.

SOURCE_STATUS.title: Enhanced Tables of Specifications for the Subjects in the Nurses Licensure Examination

questions.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
questions.STEM: A breastfeeding parent reports severe nipple pain, and the newborn makes clicking sounds with brief feeds. What should the nurse do first?
OPTIONS: Tell the parent to stop breastfeeding permanently
Advise increasing feeding intervals without observing
Assume the pain proves an infection
Observe a feeding and assess latch and transfer before recommending a change
questions.ANSWER_KEY: Observe a feeding and assess latch and transfer before recommending a change
questions.RATIONALE: Pain and clicking can reflect ineffective latch or transfer, but direct observation is needed before teaching or referral. Stopping feeding or assuming infection is premature.

Restrict fluids to prevent further vomiting
Wait for the next routine appointment

Give a detailed prognosis without assessing the client’s preferences

questions.SUBJECT: Nursing
questions.STEM: A family requests that a competent adult client not be told a serious diagnosis. What should the nurse do?

Let the family decide without the client.
Tell every relative the diagnosis.
Assess the client's preferences and rights and communicate through the appropriate professional process.

questions.RATIONALE: Confidentiality and informed participation are not displaced by family preference alone.

Ban all family discussion.

question_snapshot.SUBJECT: nursing-foundations
question_snapshot.STEM: Before administering a high-alert insulin dose, the nurse finds that the current glucose value and the medication order do not match. What is the safest action?
OPTIONS: Give the ordered dose and document the mismatch afterward
Ask the client to choose the dose
Hold administration and clarify the discrepancy using the required verification process
Delete the order from the medication record
question_snapshot.ANSWER_KEY: Hold administration and clarify the discrepancy using the required verification process
question_snapshot.RATIONALE: Pause administration and resolve the mismatch through the required verification and escalation process; do not independently change the dose or administer an order that conflicts with the available assessment. WHO’s medication-safety tool supports involving the patient or caregiver in medication conversations with health professionals, but that partnership does not let the patient choose an insulin dose or replace professional order verification.

defect_proposals.ISSUE: Stem gives 0.25 mg/kg but omits whether the amount is per dose or per day.
defect_proposals.EVIDENCE: Full stem/options/key/rationale checked; 0.25×68=17 mg is arithmetically correct under the per-dose assumption. Open RN dosage sources distinguish mg/kg/dose from mg/kg/day.
defect_proposals.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Item writer should state the intended time basis (for example, per dose) and verify the complete order context; no answer-key change until reviewed.
defect_proposals.RISK_OF_CHANGE: Changing the time basis can change the interpretation and amount prepared.

defect_proposals.ISSUE: Stem gives 15 mg/kg and asks for a liquid volume without stating the time basis.
defect_proposals.EVIDENCE: Full stem/options/key/rationale checked; 15×18=270 mg and 270/75=3.6 mL arithmetically, if 15 mg/kg is per dose. The accessible dosage-calculation sources distinguish mg/kg/dose from mg/kg/day.
defect_proposals.PROPOSED_CHANGE: Item writer should state per dose or per day and verify the intended clinical order context; do not alter the key until authorized review.
defect_proposals.RISK_OF_CHANGE: The stated basis changes whether the one-dose volume is the correct interpretation.
